title: The Ruvin
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: This is what Rabbi Yannai called Yehudah and Chizkiyah, the sons of Rabbi Chiyya, as in [Chullin 20a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.20a.2), where he said of them: “Let the ruvin receive their answer.”

In [Jerusalem Talmud Chagigah, chapter 3, end of halakhah 4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Chagigah.3.4.10): “Rabbi Yannai said: The ruvei used to say, regarding terumah prepared to the purity standard of consecrated food…”

In [Jerusalem Talmud Challah 4:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Challah.4.4.13): “Our Rabbis in the Diaspora used to separate terumah and tithes until the ruvin came and abolished it.” Who are the ruvin? The interpreters.

notes.text: The [preceding discussion in Chullin](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.19b.15) introduces the speakers as Rabbi Chiyya’s sons. The Chagigah passage discusses terumah prepared to the purity standard of consecrated food. In Challah, Rabbi Yochanan reports the practice and the text itself explains ruvin as “interpreters.” [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3224&lang=en) discusses that passage and tentatively identifies its ruvin with Rabbi Chiyya’s sons in Chullin.
